transcript_header: Date: 2027-05-20 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Location: Zoom | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (NexaHealth CTO), Ethan Shaw (Platform Eng), Priya Rao (MLOps), Samir Khan (Security)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding progress, access issues (VPC peering, S3), initial result tuning, and plan for dedicated latency benchmarks. Agreement on next steps to provision Dedicated test cluster, share traffic profile, and security doc review. Some minor transcription/call noise; references to security pack and benchmark spreadsheet.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll kick off, uh, quick check-in. duration about 45 minutes, want to cover where onboarding is at, any blockers on access, and then go over the initial tuning results we ran last week. Maya, you wanna start with status?
[00:18] Maya Patel: yeah thanks Lena, um hi all. high level we're mostly set on our side, we got the service account created, um I think the main blockers now are VPC peering and the S3 access to our sample bucket. Ethan's been trying to get the peering but IT has some routing rules.
[00:35] Ethan Shaw: yeah so we opened the peering request, but there's a couple of egress policies that our security team wants to lock down, so it's pending. also quick note, the firewall team's asking for CIDR confirmation from Redwood.
[00:50] Diego Ruiz: (Redwood SE) yep we can provide the CIDR ranges, I put them in the shared onboarding doc but I'll re-send; apologies if they landed in the wrong tab. also, for the S3 read, we asked for a temporary role; Priya, did you see that?
[01:05] Priya Rao: I saw an email, I think I didn't have permissions to attach the role. I'll follow up after.
[01:12] Lena Park: ok good. Samir, any security-side concerns we should call out?
[01:15] Samir Khan: minor questions - KMS integration and key rotation, also retention policies, where logs land. we saw the SOC2 pack but want a short summary of audit log flow.
[01:28] Lena Park: perfect, Diego and I will loop you on the security summary. Diego, quick on the peering, is there anything else we need?
[01:35] Diego Ruiz: mainly the CIDR and the service account ARN. once that's in we can validate the handshake. note: sometimes our docs call it Redwood Dedicate cluster, oops, Redwood Dedicated, and the internal name might show as 'rewood-ded' in some infra outputs - just FYI for your firewall folks.
[01:55] Maya Patel: ha, ok noted. thanks.
[02:00] Lena Park: alright next, quick review of tuning results - Diego ran a set of initial runs on hosted but we're planning Dedicated runs once peering is done. Diego, can you summarize what you saw?
[02:12] Diego Ruiz: sure, so we ran two model variants with your prompt set - one at 8k context and one at 4k - we saw latency on hosted averages of ~180-220ms per token under our sample load, cost looked inline with our earlier estimate. quality-wise Priya's prompt set showed a few hallucination modes around patient identifiers - likely prompt framing. we suggest a small prompt rewrite, and enabling a light reranking layer at the LLM output stage.
[02:45] Priya Rao: yeah we noticed that too, some outputs drop the clinical context. is the reranking something Redwood provides or we need to add our own layer?
[02:54] Diego Ruiz: we have a couple of options: you can run a lightweight reranker as a post-process in your stack, or we can enable Redwood's rerank route which does a cheap second-pass scoring. it's configurable.
[03:08] Lena Park: to add, our Optimize toolkit also has recommendations for batching and quantization for Dedicated workloads - we can share suggested profile.
[03:18] Ethan Shaw: curious on Dedicated perf numbers - how much improvement should we expect once on a dedicated GPU pool?
[03:25] Diego Ruiz: rough ballpark: Dedicated can cut tail latency and jitter significantly - e.g. from 180-220ms median to something like 60-90ms median depending on model and sequence length and kv cache hits. but that depends on batching config and how parallel your bursts are. we'll need to run the benchmark with your traffic profile to be certain.
[03:45] Maya Patel: ok good, so timeline - when can we run that benchmark?
[03:50] Diego Ruiz: once VPC peering and S3 access are done we can provision a short Dedicated instance and run the 24-48 hour benchmark. I can do the run with Ethan next week (week of 5/31).
[04:03] Priya Rao: sounds good. we have a few night-time heavy windows, we'll include those in the profile.
[04:09] Samir Khan: on compliance, we need to confirm if logs ever leave our VPC - we prefer them to land in our audited S3. is that possible?
[04:18] Diego Ruiz: yes, that's one of the supported flows. logs can be routed to your S3 via a connector, and KMS can be customer-managed. I'll put the architecture note in the security doc.
[04:30] Lena Park: great. switching gears - onboarding checklist, there were a couple of outstanding items from last call. I'll read them quickly: 1) CIDR and service account info from Redwood (Diego), 2) S3 access granted (Maya/Ethan), 3) sample prompt set and failure cases (Priya), 4) security question list (Samir). any updates on those?
[04:50] Maya Patel: we can grant S3 access by monday, I'm assigning it to Ethan.
[04:55] Ethan Shaw: yep I can do that, I'll grant the role and share the bucket path.
[04:59] Priya Rao: prompt set is mostly ready, I'll upload it to the shared folder by Friday.
[05:05] Samir Khan: I'll have the compliance Qs by Wednesday.
[05:09] Lena Park: perfect. Next: small note about observed token usage - Diego, you flagged a higher than expected token burn on a particular prompt pattern; can you elaborate?
[05:18] Diego Ruiz: yeah, one of the prompts includes an extensive system message that repeats patient context - helps with accuracy but doubles tokens. we recommended two options: condense system messages and use prefix caching, or enable KV cache longer retention on Dedicated to reduce re-sent context. there's a tradeoff with memory.
[05:40] Priya Rao: i think we can condense, we were being overly defensive in prompts. we'll try a compact form and re-run.
[05:47] Maya Patel: any quick wins on cost?
[05:50] Diego Ruiz: batching and caching are biggest wins - also inference quantization on Dedicated can reduce cost per token with small quality tradeoffs. Optimize will show model/quant profiles.
[06:05] Ethan Shaw: about quantization - are we able to do that in Private deployment? our compliance team likes the idea of Private but also wants the perf.
[06:13] Diego Ruiz: Private supports similar quantization profiles; the runtime picks kernels based on hardware. if you go Private on-prem there's an extra ops lift but possible. we'll include comparisons in the recommendation doc.
[06:30] Lena Park: okay. next, any blockers for the demo we planned for stakeholders next week?
[06:36] Maya Patel: demo depends on Dedicated results for latency numbers. if we can't run Dedicated by next Wed, might need to show hosted numbers with a caveat.
[06:45] Lena Park: understood. we'll prioritize the peering then.
[06:48] Samir Khan: quick security note - can you share the SOC2 attestation doc and a short one-pager about log retention flows? the pack was long, we just want summary bullets for our execs.
[06:58] Lena Park: yes I'll send the SOC2 summary and a one-pager. Diego will add the log flow diagram.
[07:06] Diego Ruiz: noted. also adding: in previous run, a couple transcription snafus - internal names like 'K-V cash' showed up in logs, so search terms might need normalizing when you ingest.
[07:18] Priya Rao: ha, good to know.
[07:20] Lena Park: great. let's do a quick recap - I'll read the next steps: Redwood to re-send CIDR and service account, Redwood to provide SOC2 summary + log flow one-pager, Diego to provision Dedicated test once peering is approved, Customer to grant S3 and share prompt set and traffic profile. any additions?
[07:40] Ethan Shaw: include running the latency benchmark and sharing the 48-hour spreadsheet.
[07:07] Lena Park: added.
[07:46] Maya Patel: small question: what's the cost estimate for a short Dedicated run for benchmarking?
[07:51] Diego Ruiz: for a 48-hour single Dedicated instance run it's roughly in the low thousands USD, depends on the size model. I'll break down exact numbers in the email.
[08:01] Samir Khan: for procurement we'll need that estimate and a temporary PO? Noted.
[08:06] Lena Park: ok we'll follow up with pricing. any final questions?
[08:10] Priya Rao: none from me.
[08:12] Maya Patel: no. thanks everyone.
[08:15] Lena Park: thanks all - we'll follow up with notes and the docs. meeting adjourned.
[08:20] (call ends, small crosstalk)

Notes: references shared during the call: onboarding checklist (link in drive), SOC2 pack (shared via redwood-sec link), benchmark spreadsheet (placeholder: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/nexahealth), security one-pager to be provided. Some transcription noise and mis-named internal artifacts (e.g., rewood-ded).
